<file>
00001| ---
00002| title: revalidateTag
00003| description: API Reference for the revalidateTag function.
00004| related:
00005|   links:
00006|     - app/guides/server-actions
00007| ---
00008| 
00009| `revalidateTag` allows you to invalidate cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag.
00010| 
00011| This function is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. With the recommended `max` profile, users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background.
00012| 
00013| ## Usage
00014| 
00015| `revalidateTag` can be called in Server Functions and Route Handlers.
00016| 
00017| `revalidateTag` cannot be called in Client Components or Proxy, as it only works in server environments.
00018| 
00019| ### Revalidation Behavior
00020| 
00021| Calling `revalidateTag` marks the tagged data as stale. The next request for that data kicks off a revalidation and is served stale content while it runs, using stale-while-revalidate semantics. The second argument sets how long stale content may be served. Past that, a request blocks until the revalidation completes.
00022| 
00023| - **`profile="max"` (recommended)**: A one year window, long enough that requests are always served stale content while the revalidation runs.
00024| - **Another profile, or an object**: Any other default or custom profile defined in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife), or an object with an `expire` property, when you want a different window.
00025| - **`{ expire: 0 }`**: Stale content is never served, so the next request is a blocking revalidate/cache miss. Use it when the caller needs the data gone immediately and you cannot use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag).
00026| - **No second argument (deprecated)**: Behaves like `{ expire: 0 }`. Migrate to [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions, or `profile="max"`.
00027| 
00028| The profile sets the point past which data correctness is more important than being fast.
00029| 
00030| > **Good to know**: A revalidation is triggered by a request, not by the `revalidateTag` call, so pages using the tag revalidate as they are visited rather than all at once.
00031| 
00032| ## Parameters
00033| 
00034| ```ts
00035| revalidateTag(tag: string, profile: string | { expire?: number }): void;
00036| ```
00037| 
00038| - `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to revalidate. Tags are case-sensitive and must not exceed 256 characters. A tag that exceeds the limit is never assigned to cached data, so revalidating it does nothing.
00039| - `profile`: How long stale content may be served, see [Revalidation Behavior](#revalidation-behavior). The recommended value is `"max"`. Any other default or custom profile defined in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) is also accepted, and only its `expire` is read. You can also pass an object with an `expire` property, in seconds.
00040| 
00041| Tags must first be assigned to cached data. You can do this in two ways:
00042| 
00043| - Using the [`next.tags`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) option with `fetch` for caching external API requests:
00044| 
00045| ```tsx
00046| fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })
00047| ```
00048| 
00049| - Using [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside cached functions or components with the `'use cache'` directive:
00050| 
00051| ```tsx
00052| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00053| 
00054| async function getData() {
00055|   'use cache'
00056|   cacheTag('posts')
00057|   // ...
00058| }
00059| ```
00060| 
00061| > **Good to know**: The single-argument form `revalidateTag(tag)` is deprecated. It currently works if TypeScript errors are suppressed, but this behavior may be removed in a future version. Update to the two-argument signature.
00062| 
00063| ## Returns
00064| 
00065| `revalidateTag` does not return a value.
00066| 
00067| ## Relationship with `revalidatePath`
00068| 
00069| `revalidateTag` invalidates data with specific tags across all pages that use those tags, while [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) invalidates specific page or layout paths.
00070| 
00071| > **Good to know**: These functions serve different purposes and may need to be used together for comprehensive data consistency. For detailed examples and considerations, see [relationship with revalidateTag and updateTag](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath#relationship-with-revalidatetag-and-updatetag) for more information.
00072| 
00073| ## Examples
00074| 
00075| The following examples demonstrate how to use `revalidateTag` in different contexts. In both cases, we're using `profile="max"` to mark data as stale and use stale-while-revalidate semantics, which is the recommended approach for most use cases.
00076| 
00077| ### Server Action
00078| 
00079| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
00080| 'use server'
00081| 
00082| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00083| 
00084| export default async function submit() {
00085|   await addPost()
00086|   revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
00087| }
00088| ```
00089| 
00090| ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher

00015| The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
00016| 
00017| ## Usage
00018| 
00019| To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
00020| 
00021| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
00022| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00023| 
00024| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00025|   cacheComponents: true,
00026| }
00027| 
00028| export default nextConfig
00029| ```

00031| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher

00033|   cacheComponents: true,
00034| }
00035| 
00036| module.exports = nextConfig
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
00040| 
00041| ```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
00042| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00043| 
00044| export async function getData() {
00045|   'use cache'
00046|   cacheTag('my-data')
00047|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00048|   const data = await res.json()
00049|   return data
00050| }
00051| ```
00052| 
00053| ```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
00054| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00055| 
00056| export async function getData() {
00057|   'use cache'
00058|   cacheTag('my-data')
00059|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00060|   const data = await res.json()
00061|   return data
00062| }
00063| ```

00065| You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
00066| 
00067| - Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
00068| - Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.

00074| 
00075| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00076|

00080| }
00081| ```

00084| 'use server'
00085| 
00086| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00087|

00089|   await addPost()
00090|   updateTag('my-data')
00091| }
00092| ```

00005| 
00006| > **Note:**
00007| > This API has been replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) in Next.js 16.
00008| > We recommend opting into [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and replacing `unstable_cache` with the `use cache` directive.
00009| 
00010| `unstable_cache` allows you to cache the results of expensive operations, like database queries, and reuse them across multiple requests.
00011| 
00012| ```jsx
00013| import { getUser } from './data';
00014| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
00015| 
00016| const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00017|   async (id) => getUser(id),
00018|   ['my-app-user']
00019| );
00020|

00023|   ...
00024| }
00025| ```
00026| 
00027| > **Good to know**:
00028| >
00029| > - Accessing request data such as `headers` or `cookies` inside a cache scope is not supported. Read the data outside the cached function and pass the values you need as arguments.
00030| > - This API uses Next.js' built-in cache to persist the result across requests and deployments. See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
00031| 
00032| ## Unsupported operations
00033| 
00034| The function passed to `unstable_cache` cannot depend on the incoming request. Read values from `cookies()` or `headers()` before calling the cached function, then pass those values as arguments so they become part of the cache key.

00041| - Call a function that uses the `use cache: private` directive

00049| ```

00051| - `fetchData`: This is an asynchronous function that fetches the data you want to cache. It must be a function that returns a `Promise`.

By default, `unstable_cache` already uses the arguments and the stringified version of your function as the cache key. 00001| ---
00002| title: Revalidating
00003| description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies.
00004| related:
00005|   title: API Reference
00006|   description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned on this page.
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
00009|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
00010|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
00011|     - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
00012|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath
00013| ---
00014| 
00015| > This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
00016| 
00017| Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
00018| 
00019| - **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
00020| - **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
00021| 
00022| ## `cacheLife`
00023| 
00024| [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
00025| 
00026| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
00027| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00028| 
00029| export async function getProducts() {
00030|   'use cache'
00031|   cacheLife('hours')
00032|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| `cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
00037| 
00038| | Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
00039| | --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
00040| | `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
00041| | `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
00042| | `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
00043| | `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
00044| | `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
00045| | `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
00046| | `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
00047| 
00048| For fine-grained control, pass an object:
00049| 
00050| ```tsx highlight={2-6}
00051| 'use cache'
00052| cacheLife({
00053|   stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
00054|   revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
00055|   expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
00056| })
00057| ```
00058| 
00059| > **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
00060| 
00061| See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
00062| 
00063| ## `cacheTag`
00064| 
00065| [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
00066| 
00067| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00068| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00069| 
00070| export async function getProducts() {
00071|   'use cache'
00072|   cacheTag('products')
00073|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00074| }
00075| ```
00076| 
00077| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00078| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00079| 
00080| export async function getProducts() {
00081|   'use cache'
00082|   cacheTag('products')
00083|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00084| }
00085| ```
00086| 
00087| Once tagged, invalidate the cache using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) or [`updateTag`](#updatetag).
00088| 
00089| See the [`cacheTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) to learn more.
00090| 
00091| ## `revalidateTag`
00092| 
00093| `revalidateTag` invalidates cache entries by tag using stale-while-revalidate semantics — stale content is served immediately while fresh content loads in the background. This is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, like blog posts or product catalogs.
00094| 
00095| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
00096| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00097| 
00098| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00099|   // Mutate data
00100|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00101| }
00102| ```
00103| 
00104| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00105| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00106| 
00107| export async function updateUser(id) {
00108|   // Mutate data
00109|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00110| }
00111| ```
00112| 
00113| You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00114| 
00115| > **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window.
00116| 
00117| See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
00118| 
00119| ## `updateTag`
00120| 
00121| `updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).
00122| 
00123| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
00124| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00125| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00126| 
00127| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
00128|   const post = await db.post.create({
00129|     data: {
00130|       title: formData.get('title'),
00131|       content: formData.get('content'),
00132|     },
00133|   })
00134| 
00135|   updateTag('posts')
00136|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
00141| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00142| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00143| 
00144| export async function createPost(formData) {
00145|   const post = await db.post.create({
00146|     data: {
00147|       title: formData.get('title'),
00148|       content: formData.get('content'),
00149|     },
00150|   })
00151| 
00152|   updateTag('posts')
00153|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| |              | `updateTag`                                   | `revalidateTag`                      |
00158| | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
00159| | **Where**    | Server Actions only                           | Server Actions and Route Handlers    |
00160| | **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache                     | Stale-while-revalidate               |
00161| | **Use case** | Read-your-own-writes (user sees their change) | Background refresh (slight delay OK) |
00162| 
00163| See the [`updateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) to learn more.
00164| 
00165| ## `revalidatePath`
00166| 
00167| `revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. Use it when you want to revalidate a route without knowing which tags are associated with it.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
00170| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00171| 
00172| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00173|   // Mutate data
00174|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00175| }
00176| ```
00177| 
00178| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00179| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00180| 
00181| export async function updateUser(id) {
00182|   // Mutate data
00183|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00184| }
00185| ```
00186| 
00187| > **Good to know**: Prefer tag-based revalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) over path-based when possible — it's more precise and avoids over-invalidating.
00188| 
00189| See the [`revalidatePath` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to learn more.
00190| 
00191| ## What should I cache?
00192| 
00193| Cache data that doesn't depend on [runtime data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) and that you're OK serving from cache for a period of time. Use `use cache` with `cacheLife` to describe that behavior.
00194| 
00195| When content doesn't need time-based revalidation, for example data from a CMS, use [`cacheTag`](#cachetag) and a long [`cacheLife`](#cachelife) like `max` to keep it in the static shell. Configure the content source to trigger a webhook, or other notification, that calls [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) when the content changes. This reduces unnecessary time-based revalidation for content that hasn't changed.
00196| 
00197| > **Good to know:** In serverless environments, in-memory cache entries may not persist across revalidations. See [runtime caching considerations](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations) for details.
00198|

00002| title: Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)

00004| description: Learn how to cache and revalidate data using fetch options, unstable_cache, and route segment configs for projects not using Cache Components.
00005| ---
00006| 
00007| > This guide assumes you are **not** using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) which was introduced in version 16 under the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents).
00008| 
00009| ## Caching `fetch` requests
00010| 
00011| By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
00012| 
00013| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00014| export default async function Page() {
00015|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
00016| }
00017| ```
00018| 
00019| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00020| export default async function Page() {
00021|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
00022| }
00023| ```
00024| 
00025| See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
00026| 
00027| ### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
00028| 
00029| `unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
00030| 
00031| ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00032| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00033| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00034| 
00035| export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00036|   async (id: string) => {
00037|     return db
00038|       .select()
00039|       .from(users)
00040|       .where(eq(users.id, id))
00041|       .then((res) => res[0])
00042|   },
00043|   ['user'], // cache key prefix
00044|   {
00045|     tags: ['user'],
00046|     revalidate: 3600,
00047|   }
00048| )
00049| ```
00050| 
00051| ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00052| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00053| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00054| 
00055| export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00056|   async (id) => {
00057|     return db
00058|       .select()
00059|       .from(users)
00060|       .where(eq(users.id, id))
00061|       .then((res) => res[0])
00062|   },
00063|   ['user'], // cache key prefix
00064|   {
00065|     tags: ['user'],
00066|     revalidate: 3600,
00067|   }
00068| )
00069| ```
00070| 
00071| The third argument accepts:
00072| 
00073| - `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
00074| - `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
00075| 
00076| See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
00077| 
00078| ### Route segment config
00079| 
00080| You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00081| 
00082| #### `dynamic`
00083| 
00084| Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
00085| 
00086| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00087| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00088| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00089| ```
00090| 
00091| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00092| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00093| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
00097| - **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
00098|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
00099|   - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
00100| - **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
00101|   - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
00102|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
00103|   - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
00104| - **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
00105| 
00106| #### `fetchCache`
00107| 
00108| <details>
00109|   <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
00110| 
00111| A `fetch` request that sets no `cache` option is fetched once during `next build` if it is reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used, because the route is prerendered up to that point. Requests discovered **after** a Request-time API run on every request.
00112| 
00113| `fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00116| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00117| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00118| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00119| ```
00120| 
00121| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00122| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00123| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00124| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00125| ```
00126| 
00127| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
00128| - **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
00129| - **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.

00115| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher

00117| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00118| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00119| ```
00120| 
00121| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00122| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00123| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00124| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00125| ```
00126| 
00127| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
00128| - **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
00129| - **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
00130| - **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
00131| - **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
00132| - **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`

00134| 
00135| ##### Cross-route segment behavior
00136| 
00137| - Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
00138|   - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. 00140|     - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00141|     - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00142|   - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.

00145| </details>
00146| 
00147| ## Time-based revalidation
00148| 
00149| Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
00150| 
00151| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00152| export default async function Page() {
00153|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00158| export default async function Page() {
00159|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00160| }
00161| ```
00162| 
00163| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00164| 
00165| ### Route segment config `revalidate`
00166| 
00167| Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00170| export const revalidate = false
00171| // false | 0 | number
00172| ```
00173| 
00174| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00175| export const revalidate = false
00176| // false | 0 | number
00177| ```
00178| 
00179| - **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
00180| - **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of `fetch` requests that do not set a `cache` option to `'no-store'` but leaves `fetch` requests that opt into `'force-cache'` or use a positive `revalidate` as is.
00181| - **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
00182| 
00183| > **Good to know**:
00184| >
00185| > - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
00186| > - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
00187| > - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
00188| 
00189| #### Revalidation frequency
00190| 
00191| - The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
00192| - Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
00193| 
00194| ## On-demand revalidation
00195|

00019| 
00020| A **Server Action** is a [React Server Function](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) invoked through React's action mechanisms, such as `<form action>`, `<button formAction>`, or a client-side transition.
00021| 
00022| You create one by adding the [`'use server'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-server) directive, then invoke it from a form, or from an event handler or `useEffect` wrapped in `startTransition`. For the basics of creating and invoking Server Functions, see [Mutating data](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) and the [Forms guide](/docs/app/guides/forms).
00023| 
00024| This page covers the parts of Server Actions that are specific to Next.js: how they commonly map to mutations, how the response carries both returned data and re-rendered UI, how the client dispatches them, the security boundary the framework enforces, and the configuration available.
00025| 
00026| ## Sequential dispatch on the client
00027| 
00028| Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client. If a user triggers three actions in quick succession, the second waits for the first to finish, then the third waits for the second. This keeps the re-rendered server tree consistent with the action result that produced it.
00029| 
00030| A consequence: do not rely on `Promise.all` to parallelize Server Actions from the client. If you need parallel work, do it inside a single Server Action, fetch in parallel from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#server-components), or use a [Route Handler](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend#manipulating-data) for non-mutation requests.
00031| 
00032| > **Good to know:** This is a property of the client dispatcher, not of Server Functions in general. Server-side, an action runs in its own request and can do anything an async function can do.
00033| 
00034| ## A single response carries data and UI
00035| 
00036| When a Server Action triggers an immediate revalidation, Next.js does the work inside one HTTP request: it runs the action, then re-renders the current route server-side. The response that comes back contains both pieces in the same Flight stream:
00037| 
00038| - The action's return value, consumed by `useActionState` or the awaited promise on the client.
00039| - A newly rendered [RSC Payload](/docs/app/glossary#rsc-payload) for the current route, which the client commits as a seeded navigation.
00040| 
00041| Your application code does not need a follow-up fetch to see the updated UI for the current page.
00042| 
00043| A re-render is included in the same response when the action does any of these:
00044| 
00045| - Calls [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to immediately invalidate cached data.
00046| - Calls [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) to refetch the current route's RSC Payload.
00047| - Mutates cookies through [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies#understanding-cookie-behavior-in-server-functions). Setting or deleting a cookie automatically re-renders the current page so the UI reflects the new value.
00048| - Calls [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect). The response navigates the router and streams the destination's RSC Payload.
00049| 
00050| ```ts filename="app/posts/actions.ts"
00051| 'use server'
00052| 
00053| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00054| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00055| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00056| 
00057| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
00058|   const session = await auth()
00059|   if (!session?.user) throw new Error('Unauthorized')
00060| 
00061|   await db.post.create({
00062|     data: {
00063|       title: String(formData.get('title')),
00064|       authorId: session.user.id,
00065|     },
00066|   })
00067| 
00068|   revalidatePath('/posts')
00069| }
00070| ```
00071| 
00072| The mutation, the cache invalidation, and the page re-render all complete in a single roundtrip. Because [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect#behavior) throws a control-flow exception, any code after it does not run. Place revalidation calls before `redirect` if the destination needs the fresh data.
00073| 
00074| [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) with a stale-while-revalidate profile is the exception: it marks the tag for background refresh and does **not** include a re-render in the action response. The page reflects the change on a later read. An action that does none of the above carries only its return value, and the current route is not re-rendered.
00075| 
00076| ## Security
00077| 
00078| A Server Action runs as a POST request against the page that invokes it. At build time, the `'use server'` directive tells the compiler to swap the function's implementation in client bundles for a reference (an action ID plus a dispatcher) that POSTs back to the server. The implementation stays on the server, but the route is reachable to anyone who can send the same POST. Treat every action as an untrusted entry point.
00079| 
00080| Next.js enforces a few framework-level protections:
00081| 
00082| - **CSRF check.** The request's `Origin` is compared to the `Host` (or `X-Forwarded-Host`). Mismatches are rejected. Configure [`serverActions.allowedOrigins`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverActions#allowedorigins) for proxy or CDN domains.
00083| - **Body size limit.** Action requests are capped at 1MB by default. Configure [`serverActions.bodySizeLimit`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverActions#bodysizelimit) when accepting larger payloads.
00084| - **Encrypted action IDs and dead code elimination.** Action references are encrypted at build time, and unused Server Functions are stripped from client bundles so they have no public endpoint. See [Built-in Server Actions security features](/docs/app/guides/data-security#built-in-server-actions-security-features).
00085| - **Closure variable encryption.** Variables captured by an inline action are encrypted before being sent to the client. For multi-instance and self-hosted deployments, set `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to a stable key shared across instances. See [Closures and encryption](/docs/app/guides/data-security#closures-and-encryption).
00086| 
00087| Framework protections are not a substitute for application-level checks. Inside every action:
00088| 
00089| - **Authenticate and authorize.** Render-time gating (only rendering a form on an authenticated page) is not a security boundary, because requests can be sent without going through the UI.

00091| - **Constrain return values.** Action returns are serialized to the client. Shape them to what the UI renders, not raw database records.
00092| 
00093| For end-to-end patterns including a Data Access Layer, return-value tainting, and rate limiting, see the [Data Security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security#mutating-data).
00094| 
00095| Destructive operations like deletes may warrant stronger handling, such as elevated session checks or re-authentication, and a loud failure when those checks miss.
00096| 
00097| ```ts filename="app/posts/actions.ts" highlight={6,7,8}
00098| 'use server'
00099| 
00100| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00101| 
00102| export async function deletePost(postId: string) {
00103|   const session = await auth()
00104|   if (!session?.user) throw new Error('Unauthorized')
00105|   if (!(await canDelete(session.user, postId))) throw new Error('Forbidden')
00106| 
00107|   await db.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } })
00108| }
00109| ```
00110| 
00111| If you've enabled the experimental [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts) flag, you can throw [`unauthorized()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized) and [`forbidden()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/forbidden) from `next/navigation` instead, so Next.js renders the corresponding `unauthorized.tsx` / `forbidden.tsx` UI segment automatically.
00112| 
00113| For example, a client legitimately tells the server _which_ item to act on, but it should not supply the row's contents or ownership. Send a reference (typically an ID) plus the user's change, and re-read the rest from a trusted source using the session. Schema validation (zod or similar) only checks the _shape_ of the input. A well-formed `Item` object can still refer to a row the caller does not own.
00114| 
00115| ```ts filename="app/items/actions.ts"
00116| 'use server'
00117| 
00118| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00119| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00120| 
00121| // Unsafe: no auth, no ownership check. The whole item, including its id, comes
00122| // from the client, so anyone who can POST here can mark any item complete.
00123| export async function completeItemUnsafe(item: Item) {
00124|   await db.item.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { completed: true } })
00125| }
00126| 
00127| // Safe: take only the change, derive identity from the session, look up by ownership.
00128| export async function completeItem(itemId: string) {
00129|   const session = await auth()
00130|   if (!session?.user) return
00131| 
00132|   const item = await db.item.findFirst({
00133|     where: { id: itemId, ownerId: session.user.id },
00134|   })
00135|   if (!item) return
00136| 
00137|   await db.item.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { completed: true } })
00138| }
00139| ```
00140| 
00141| ## Choosing a cache update
00142| 
00143| After mutating data, on-demand revalidation updates the server cache, the client router, or both. Choose based on what needs to change:
00144| 
00145| - [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag): immediate expiration of a tag. The next read (including the route re-render that ships with the action's response) waits for fresh data. Use when the action needs **read-your-own-writes** so the user immediately sees their change. Server Actions only.
00146| - [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag): stale-while-revalidate refresh of a tag with a cache-life profile. Subsequent reads get the stale value while a fresh fetch happens in the background, so the action's own re-render does **not** wait for the new data.
00147| - [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath): invalidate by URL path. Use when one route is affected and tagging is overkill.
00148| - [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh): refetch the current route's RSC Payload without invalidating cached data. Use when the view depends on state outside the cache that the action just changed.
00149| 
00150| When `updateTag`, `revalidatePath`, or `refresh` runs, Next.js re-renders the current route server-side and includes a newly rendered [RSC Payload](/docs/app/glossary#rsc-payload) in the action's response, so the page reflects the change in the same roundtrip. `revalidateTag` with a stale-while-revalidate profile intentionally skips that immediate re-render.

00026| ## Sequential dispatch on the client

00028| Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client. If a user triggers three actions in quick succession, the second waits for the first to finish, then the third waits for the second. This keeps the re-rendered server tree consistent with the action result that produced it.

00030| A consequence: do not rely on `Promise.all` to parallelize Server Actions from the client. 00031|

00033| - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
00034| - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
00035| 
00036| > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 00038| Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. 00041|

00043|

00045| 
00046| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
